## Current research

### Engineering sunflower lipid metabolism

**ANRF-funded project (CRG/2023/006573)**  
*Engineering sunflower for increased triacylglycerol (TAG) content and altered fatty acid profile using genome editing and chia genes*

My current research at the University of Hyderabad focuses on engineering sunflower lipid metabolism to increase TAG accumulation and alter fatty-acid composition, including enrichment of oil with omega-3 fatty acids.

My work combines:

- CRISPR/Cas9 and gRNA strategy design
- Cloning and genome-editing vector construction
- Sunflower transformation and tissue-culture workflows
- Regeneration protocol development and optimisation
- PCR-based genotyping and gene-expression analysis
- GC-MS/MS method development and quantitative lipid profiling
- Instrument maintenance and troubleshooting

### Lipid metabolism and metabolic regulation

My broader research interests centre on how lipid biosynthetic pathways are regulated and how metabolic engineering can alter storage-lipid accumulation and fatty-acid composition.

Key interests include:

- TAG biosynthesis and DGAT2
- Fatty-acid desaturation and FAD genes
- Omega-3 fatty-acid enrichment
- Lipid metabolic heterogeneity
- Integrative multi-omics

### Mass spectrometry and analytical biochemistry

I have hands-on experience in LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS across research and regulated bioanalytical environments. At Axis Clinicals, I worked across 34 BA/BE projects, developed 5 bioanalytical methods and validated 14 methods across 15 studies.

I am interested in extending mass-spectrometry workflows toward lipidomics, metabolomics, and molecular profiling.

### Molecular biology and genome engineering

My molecular biology interests include CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, cloning, PCR, genotyping, gene-expression analysis, nucleic-acid isolation, plant transformation, and tissue culture.

### Computational biology

I use and am developing experience with NCBI-BLAST, Primer3, CHOP-CHOP, IGV, Jalview, AutoDock Vina, GROMACS, PyMOL, Python, R, and Linux.
